usmle-2026-0025.subject: Pharmacology
usmle-2026-0025.question: The antidote's protective effect against hepatocellular necrosis is best explained by which of the following mechanisms?
usmle-2026-0025.chosenText: Competitively inhibiting CYP2E1 so the parent drug is excreted unchanged
usmle-2026-0025.answerText: Replenishing hepatic glutathione stores used to conjugate a reactive electrophilic metabolite

usmle-2026-0027.subject: Microbiology
usmle-2026-0027.question: Which characteristic of the responsible organism most directly accounts for his hemoptysis and the CT findings?
usmle-2026-0027.chosenText: Germ-tube-forming yeast that invades along mucosal surfaces
usmle-2026-0027.answerText: Angioinvasion by septate hyphae that branch at acute angles, causing vascular thrombosis and hemorrhagic infarction

usmle-2026-0030.subject: Pediatrics
usmle-2026-0030.question: Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
usmle-2026-0030.chosenText: Immediate plasma exchange as first-line therapy
usmle-2026-0030.answerText: Supportive care with careful fluid and electrolyte management, avoiding antibiotics and antimotility agents

usmle-2026-0037.subject: Pathology
usmle-2026-0037.type: Chronic Passive Hepatic Congestion (centrilobular / zone 3 necrosis)
usmle-2026-0037.question: Which of the following best explains why this histologic pattern is centered on the central veins rather than the portal tracts?
usmle-2026-0037.chosenText: A one-way valve in the sinusoidal capillary bed shields portal-tract hepatocytes from any rise in central venous pressure
usmle-2026-0037.answerText: Central-vein hepatocytes are the last in the sinusoidal flow to receive oxygen and are the first to bear the retrograde rise in venous pressure from right heart failure

usmle-2026-0038.subject: Pharmacology
usmle-2026-0038.question: Which of the following best explains the mechanism by which glucagon reverses this patient's bradycardia and hypotension?
usmle-2026-0038.chosenText: Glucagon directly opens myocardial L-type calcium channels, raising intracellular calcium independent of any second messenger
usmle-2026-0038.answerText: Glucagon binds its own Gs-coupled receptor on cardiac myocytes, activating adenylate cyclase and raising intracellular cAMP independent of the blocked beta-adrenergic receptor

usmle-2026-0039.subject: Physiology
usmle-2026-0039.type: ACE Inhibitor-Induced AKI in Bilateral Renal Artery Stenosis
usmle-2026-0039.question: Which of the following best explains the mechanism of this acute decline in renal function?
usmle-2026-0039.chosenText: Lisinopril directly constricts the afferent arteriole, reducing total renal blood flow independent of angiotensin II
usmle-2026-0039.answerText: Loss of angiotensin II-mediated efferent arteriolar constriction removes the compensatory mechanism maintaining glomerular filtration pressure distal to the stenoses

usmle-2026-0041.subject: Neurology
usmle-2026-0041.type: Guillain-Barré Syndrome — Respiratory Monitoring Before Definitive Therapy
usmle-2026-0041.question: Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate next step in management?
usmle-2026-0041.chosenText: Start intravenous immunoglobulin immediately, without further assessment of respiratory status
usmle-2026-0041.answerText: Admit for close monitoring of forced vital capacity (FVC) and negative inspiratory force to anticipate respiratory failure

usmle-2026-0044.subject: Biochemistry
usmle-2026-0044.question: Which of the following best explains the absence of ketosis in this hypoglycemic child?
usmle-2026-0044.chosenText: Deficient HMG-CoA lyase activity blocks the terminal step of ketone body synthesis
usmle-2026-0044.answerText: Deficient medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase activity blocks beta-oxidation of medium-chain fatty acids, limiting the acetyl-CoA available for ketogenesis

usmle-2026-0045.subject: Microbiology
usmle-2026-0045.question: Which of the following is the most appropriate next diagnostic test to confirm the suspected diagnosis?
usmle-2026-0045.chosenText: Sputum acid-fast bacillus smear and culture for suspected tuberculosis
usmle-2026-0045.answerText: Urinary antigen test for Legionella pneumophila serogroup 1

usmle-2026-0046.subject: Internal Medicine
usmle-2026-0046.question: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
usmle-2026-0046.chosenText: Intravenous adenosine to attempt pharmacologic termination of the rhythm
usmle-2026-0046.answerText: Rate control with an intravenous beta-blocker as the initial step in management

usmle-2026-0043.subject: Immunology
usmle-2026-0043.question: Which of the following best describes the mechanism underlying this infant's disease?
usmle-2026-0043.chosenText: Global arrest of lymphocyte development due to adenosine deaminase deficiency
usmle-2026-0043.answerText: Arrest of B-cell maturation at the pre-B stage due to a defective Bruton tyrosine kinase

usmle-2026-0104.question: Impaired activity of which of the following enzymes is the most likely cause of this patient's condition?
